entry.title: Open MPC Plugin Manager 2.1.0
entry.summary: **Plugin Manager 2.1.0** - **Open it from MENU.** With the new Plugin Manager App (released separately as `plugin-manager-app-v2.1.0`), MENU gets a "Plugin Manager" tile that opens the Manager full screen, with its own tab bar along the bottom. You no longer need to put the plugin on a track to use it. MPC OS 3.10.1 on Gen2 (tested on a Live III). - **Six cards per page** on PLUGINS in that full-screen view, and the footer status text fits. - **Addins install Addin Restore for you.** On a Gen2 M

entry.title: Open MPC Plugin Manager 2.0.0
entry.summary: **Plugin Manager 2.0.0** - **Progress on the MPC's screen.** While MPC is stopped for an update, the screen now shows what's happening: "Installing Model-72 1.0.0", step 2 of 5, a moving bar and "Don't switch the MPC off". Then "Starting MPC". No more dark screen. On Gen2 it uses Akai's own splash, and the screen is handed back before MPC starts. - **Safe if the power goes.** Each step is written to a journal on the settings drive. entry.title: Open MPC Plugin Manager 1.3.5
entry.summary: Browse the OpenMPC catalog and install, update and remove plugins on the MPC itself, with rollback; for Gen1 and Gen2. ## Requirements - A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61). The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested. - **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit. - Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up

entry.title: Open MPC Plugin Manager 1.3.2
entry.summary: ## What's new in 1.3.2 - **Background server on Gen1** (Force, MPC Live / One / X on MPC OS 3.9.x): the SETTINGS toggle now installs the daemon as a system service, so the web page is served at boot. New in this release and not yet tested on a Gen1 device: back up first. - Thumbnails for 45 more catalog plugins. - The installer (`install.sh`) now picks the right plugin folder on MPC OS 3.10.1+ by itself (the existing `VST2 Plugins` copy), so an upgrade no longer leaves the old copy loading. - Fi
